title: Rebase requirements against the assessment brief
outcome: Record the binding JDBC/JCash requirements and the scope cut line.
checkpoint: Which supplied requirements are mandatory, and which sample features are only examples?
acceptance: Assessment alignment document exists; database, login, cash-in, transfer, history, and screenshot requirements are traceable; upgrades are explicitly deferred.

title: Create validated bank account state
outcome: Keep a valid account identifier, holder name, and private PHP balance.
checkpoint: What invalid constructor state must be rejected before an object exists?
acceptance: Private state; valid construction; no negative opening balance; learner explains each invariant.

title: Implement validated deposits
outcome: Add a positive, precision-safe deposit rule.
checkpoint: Why must validation occur before balance mutation?
acceptance: Positive amount succeeds; null, zero, negative, and excessive precision reject without balance change.

title: Implement validated withdrawals
outcome: Add a withdrawal rule that rejects invalid and insufficient-fund amounts.
checkpoint: Which condition prevents an overdraft and how will you prove no mutation on failure?
acceptance: Valid withdrawal succeeds; invalid/over-balance request rejects without balance change.

title: Write regression tests for the current account rules
outcome: Turn existing account predictions into focused JUnit tests before integrating persistence.
checkpoint: Which assertions prove a rejected operation did not change balance?
acceptance: Tests cover construction, deposit, withdrawal, and at least one unchanged-state failure; test command passes.

title: Add assessment models and package structure
outcome: Define User, Transaction, TransactionType, and the required package structure without duplicating account state.
checkpoint: Which object owns user identity, current balance access, and a transaction record?
acceptance: Model classes have private fields, constructors and accessors; BankAccount is moved only after tests protect it; model/service/util structure is visible.

title: Configure JDBC and create the local schema
outcome: Create a PostgreSQL connection utility and schema for synthetic users and transactions.
checkpoint: Why do connection details belong in configuration, not in a Swing frame?
acceptance: JDBC driver/configuration is documented without committed secrets; connection succeeds; users and transactions tables have primary keys and required columns.

title: Persist and retrieve users through JDBC
outcome: Implement user save/find/authentication lookup behind a repository boundary.
checkpoint: How does a ResultSet become a User without SQL leaking into LoginService?
acceptance: Seeded synthetic user can be saved/read; missing user is handled explicitly; balance retrieval matches stored data.

title: Persist transactions through JDBC
outcome: Store and query cash-in and transfer records by user.
checkpoint: Which transaction fields prove who did what and when?
acceptance: Successful activity is persisted with type, amount, details, timestamp, and user link; per-user query returns only that user's records.

title: Implement three-attempt mobile and PIN login
outcome: Authenticate a seeded local user by mobile number and PIN with a maximum of three attempts.
checkpoint: Where is attempt counting kept, and what ends the login interaction?
acceptance: Correct credentials return the stored user; invalid credentials show a readable failure; third failure stops the attempt flow.

title: Expose the stored balance through a service
outcome: Return the successfully logged-in user's stored balance without UI-side calculation.
checkpoint: Why should the dashboard read stored state rather than keep an unrelated display value?
acceptance: Login-to-balance flow reads the same persisted balance; an unavailable user is handled clearly.

title: Implement persistent cash-in
outcome: Accept a positive amount, update stored balance, and add a cash-in record.
checkpoint: What must be true if the balance update succeeds but the transaction insert fails?
acceptance: Positive cash-in persists balance and log together; invalid amount leaves both unchanged; result can be re-read after restart.

title: Implement persistent transfers
outcome: Transfer money to an existing receiver mobile number using one JDBC transaction.
checkpoint: Which checks happen before mutation, and why is rollback needed?
acceptance: Recipient, positive amount, and sender funds are validated; sender/receiver balances and transfer logs update together; rejected transfer changes nothing.

title: Implement per-user transaction history
outcome: Return a logged-in user's cash-in and transfer logs in a readable order.
checkpoint: How does the query prevent one user from seeing another user's history?
acceptance: History contains the expected type, amount, details, and time for one user only.

title: Create the local integration smoke flow
outcome: Wire a bounded synthetic scenario in Main to prove services work before Swing screens.
checkpoint: Which outputs prove login, balance change, transfer, and history without pretending Main owns rules?
acceptance: Main composes dependencies and prints an explainable smoke result; no SQL or banking arithmetic is copied into Main.

title: Design the required Swing workflow
outcome: Sketch the login, dashboard, operation, and history states before UI coding.
checkpoint: What does each screen show after success and after an expected failure?
acceptance: Simple screen map identifies mobile/PIN login, balance, cash-in, transfer, history, feedback, and logout/reset state.

title: Build the Swing login screen
outcome: Connect mobile/PIN inputs and three-attempt feedback to LoginService.
checkpoint: How does the frame reset only after a successful login or a locked attempt flow?
acceptance: Successful login opens the selected user's dashboard; invalid and third-attempt messages are visible; no credential is printed/logged.

title: Display the persisted account dashboard
outcome: Show the logged-in user's name and current stored balance.
checkpoint: When must the UI refresh its displayed balance?
acceptance: Dashboard shows identity and balance from service data, not hard-coded text.

title: Connect the cash-in Swing flow
outcome: Allow a logged-in user to cash in and receive immediate readable feedback.
checkpoint: How do UI validation and service validation work together?
acceptance: Valid cash-in refreshes balance; invalid input shows a clear error and does not mutate persisted state.

title: Connect the transfer Swing flow
outcome: Allow transfer by receiver mobile number with validation feedback.
checkpoint: Which details make a transfer success or failure understandable in a screenshot?
acceptance: Valid transfer refreshes sender balance; missing receiver, invalid amount, and insufficient funds are clearly rejected.

title: Connect the transaction-history Swing flow
outcome: Display the current user's cash-in and transfer history.
checkpoint: How can you show that the history is user-specific and persistent?
acceptance: History view shows required transaction fields for the logged-in user and remains after relaunch.

title: Polish expected-error and reset behaviour
outcome: Make normal success, validation error, and logout/reset paths consistent and readable.
checkpoint: Which errors are business feedback versus unexpected faults?
acceptance: No stack trace is shown as normal user feedback; logout/reset safely clears displayed user state; core screens remain usable.

title: Record bounded performance evidence
outcome: Document the small performance checks appropriate to this local assessment app.
checkpoint: What can you honestly measure without pretending this is a production load test?
acceptance: Connection reuse/configuration, query scope, and observed local flow timing are recorded; no unsupported performance claims.

title: Run the assessment regression walkthrough
outcome: Verify each required flow using stable synthetic data.
checkpoint: What exact evidence proves each rubric row, including a rejected attempt?
acceptance: Tests and manual walkthrough cover login attempts, balance, cash-in, transfer, history, persistence, and user feedback.

title: Write the truthful assessment README and explanation
outcome: Explain actual architecture, setup, data model, commands, and limitations.
checkpoint: Which claims can the repository and screenshots prove?
acceptance: README names Java, Swing, JDBC, PostgreSQL, and actual implemented flows; no feature is claimed without evidence.

title: Capture rubric-mapped screenshots
outcome: Capture readable screenshots that prove each required behaviour.
checkpoint: Which caption explains what each image proves?
acceptance: Screenshots include login, balance, cash-in, transfer, history, and persistence/validation evidence with fictional data.

title: Assemble and inspect the final submission PDF
outcome: Create the screenshot PDF and visually verify it before submission.
checkpoint: Can a reviewer map every screenshot to an implemented requirement?
acceptance: PDF is readable, uses correct identity details, contains only synthetic data, and is visually checked.

title: Plan the Spring portfolio upgrade
outcome: Map the proven assessment domain and persistence boundary into a Spring Boot web upgrade.
checkpoint: What will Spring replace, and what Java/JDBC rules remain reusable?
acceptance: Upgrade plan keeps tested services/repositories as evidence; no Spring work begins before assessment submission.

title: Prioritize portfolio hardening after submission
outcome: Choose the next honest upgrade: admin roles, password security, Docker, deployment, or a React evaluation.
checkpoint: Which upgrade creates the strongest evidence for the time available?
acceptance: One scoped next upgrade is selected with risks and evidence criteria; no technology is added merely for a keyword.
